overview: From 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-18, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 24 new PRs (23 merged), 6 new issues, and 25 active contributors.

topIssues.title: op-service/txmgr: move test and dev L1s to Osaka, then delete the blob-proof path
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
txmgr chooses between blob proofs (sidecar v0) and cell proofs (v1, EIP-7594) by `CellProofTime`. The public L1s (mainnet, Sepolia, Hoodi) all activated Osaka in Oct–Dec 2025. The clients handle the two sidecar versions as follows:

- **reth, after Osaka:** rejects v0 sidecars (`UnexpectedEip4844SidecarAfterOsaka`).
- **go-ethereum, after Osaka:** converts v0 to v1 at `eth_sendRawTransaction`, but only for a transition period (`TODO: remove in go-ethereum v1.17.x`).
- **Both, before Osaka:** v1 transactions never get into a block. go-ethereum's block builder asks its pool for v0 transactions, and that pool holds v1 only. op-geth and reth reject v1 sidecars.

So the blob-proof path only serves pre-Osaka L1s, and today those are our own test and dev L1s.

## Plan

The test L1s move first, using only the existing cell-proof settings. The production changes then need no test churn.

1. [x] **#24186**: moves the op-e2e system blob tests to an Osaka L1. (Seb)
2. [x] **#24216**: test L1s to Osaka:
   - action tests and kona's Go proofs tests: default L1 at Osaka (`op-e2e/e2eutils/setup.go`), and the action batcher sends cell proofs by default
   - fork-transition tests (`dencun_fork`, `ecotone_fork`, kona `l1_blob_parameter_forks`, `l1_prague_fork`, `pectra_blob_schedule`): keep their pre-Osaka L1 segment, since nodes syncing from genesis still derive from Cancun- and Prague-era L1 blocks, but post blobs only from Osaka on
   - the op-deployer L1 dev genesis and the op-e2e system default L1 start at Osaka
   - every test txmgr sends cell proofs: `setuputils.NewTxMgrConfig` stops pinning `CellProofTime: math.MaxUint64`
   - the Prague Anvil op-deployer test posts no blobs, so it is out of scope
3. [x] **#24211**: txmgr sends cell proofs by default on every L1.
4. [ ] **#24213**: txmgr and txplan send cell proofs only, and `--txmgr.cell-proof-time` is deleted outright. It also deletes:
   - the action batcher's `EnableCellProofs` option
   - the action L1 miner's pre-Osaka sidecar check: it now requires Osaka for a blob transaction
   - what #24186 adds: `useCellProofs()`, the `CellProofTime` block in `e2esys/setup.go`, and `CreateEmptyBlobTx`'s `cellProofs` parameter
5. [ ] Confirm that no supported chain settles on a pre-Osaka L1.
6. [x] ~~**#24212**: delete the deprecated flag after a release.~~ #24213 deletes it outright.

Related: #24172.

topIssues.title: op-service/txmgr: delete the deprecated --txmgr.cell-proof-time flag
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
After #24210, txmgr builds cell-proof sidecars only and ignores `--txmgr.cell-proof-time` (`*_TXMGR_CELL_PROOF_TIME`). The flag is hidden: setting it logs a warning, and a time in the future fails at startup, because that operator expects blob proofs.

Once a release of op-batcher, op-proposer and op-challenger has shipped with that warning, delete:

- the `txmgr.cell-proof-time` flag, `CellProofTimeFlagName`, and `CLIConfig.CellProofTime` in `op-service/txmgr/cli.go`
- the warning in `NewConfig`, the future-time check in `CLIConfig.Check`, and their tests

`opql` (`acceptance-tests/opqlnode/fusaka_test.go`) sets `CellProofTime`; it needs updating when it next bumps op-service.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P against kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

[`TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/reorg/sync_test.go) is skipped when the acceptance suite runs against kona-node.

Kona times out waiting for the expected unsafe-head reorg after CL P2P connectivity is restored.

## Required work

Reproduce the P2P restoration path, distinguish test synchronization from Kona unsafe-queue/reorg behavior, fix the responsible layer, and remove the Kona skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause and resolution are documented.
- [ ] `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P` no longer skips when `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`.
- [ ] After CL P2P is restored, Kona fills the gap and converges on the expected unsafe chain.
- [ ] Existing op-node coverage continues to pass.

## Related

- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18676
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17694
- Parent inventory: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/101

topIssues.title: kona-gossip: Record dial and connection counts as counters, not gauges
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
kona-gossip records several counts as gauges, although they only ever go up. Found while working on #23661.

### Affected metrics
For example `kona_node_dial_peer`, `kona_node_dial_peer_error{type}` and `kona_node_gossipsub_connection{type}`. They're described with `describe_gauge!` ([metrics/mod.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/metrics/mod.rs#L87)) and incremented with `metrics::gauge!(..).increment(1)` ([driver.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/driver.rs#L324)). op-node uses counters for the same things: `op_node_<proc>_p2p_dials{allow}` and `accepts` are `CounterVec`s.

### Proposal
- Switch each of these to `counter!` / `describe_counter!`, including the zeroing in `Metrics::zero()`. Do each metric completely, or a gauge and a counter end up sharing one name.
- The names can stay: kona's exporter (`PrometheusBuilder::new()` in kona-cli) doesn't add a `_total` suffix, and the Grafana dashboards in `rust/kona/docker/recipes/*/grafana/dashboards/overview.json` already use `rate()` on them. Owners of external dashboards and alerts should still hear about it, since some backends store the metric type.

### Related: `already_connected` isn't an error
`kona_node_dial_peer_error{type="already_connected"}` mostly counts discovery handing over the ENRs of peers we're already connected to, which happens all the time. The "Peers Dialed / min" panel plots it next to real errors. The network actor's ENR branch ([actor.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/network/actor.rs#L145)) shouldn't call `dial` for a connected peer at all, which would leave the label for actual mistakes.

topPRs.title: kona-peers,kona-disc,kona-gossip!: Keep confirmed peers in the bootstore
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

The bootstore records how each saved peer was confirmed, and a full store keeps the confirmed ones. Second PR of a stack for #23767, on top of #24155.

For operators:
- The file is `{"version": 1, "records": [...]}`, one record per node, with `udp_verified_at` (a discovery session that lasted five minutes) and `tcp_verified_at` (gossip dialed the node at its record's TCP address). Old files, a plain list, are read and rewritten.
- A full store evicts unconfirmed records first and peers gossip reached last, so sessions under fresh keys no longer push out peers that work.
- A public-only node no longer dials back a private node that started a session with it; the private node dials, and can redial. `kona_node_discovery_events{type="session_established"}` no longer counts those sessions.
- Saved records without a TCP address are no longer handed to gossip, which counted a dial error for each every minute.

BREAKING CHANGE: the bootstore file format changes; earlier kona-node versions fail on it at startup, so delete the file to go back. In kona-peers, `BootStore::open` returns only the store, `SkippedEntry` and `SkipReason` are gone, `valid_peers_with_chain_id` returns an iterator, and `BootStoreError` has a `NewerVersion` variant.

### Why

The bootstore saved every session's record, with nothing to tell a peer that worked from one that never did, and evicted the oldest when full. Anyone starting sessions under fresh keys could replace every saved peer, so that after a restart the node would bootstrap from the attacker's records.

### How

- Evidence is only what the node saw itself. A session counts once discv5 still holds it after five minutes, which means it answered a ping, much as geth saves a node only after several. A connection counts only if we dialed it: op-node dials from its listen port, so an inbound connection can come from the record's address without showing that we can reach it.
- Among unconfirmed sessions, the youngest is evicted first, as the attacker picks the rate of fresh ones. Ties are broken at random, not by node ID, which keys can be ground for.
- Dialing back without saving, from #23766, is reverted: a node that dials a record it doesn't save can never redial it, and its dial can leave the other node with only an inbound connection, which confirms nothing.

### Caveats

- The per-/24 limit on the store is deferred to #23764: one host with many keys can still fill it with records whose addresses work.
- Evidence uses wall-clock time, so a large clock jump can count a fresh session as lasted.
- Evidence doesn't expire yet; that's a later PR.

### Alternatives

- An invalid entry is skipped with `serde_with::VecSkipError` and logged with serde's error, rather than parsed entry by entry to log its content.
- Review agents run: `rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer`; each fix has its own commit. Dismissed: the invalid-entry WARN not naming the file or the entry, moving gossip's private `tcp_socket` to kona-peers, and the Korean configuration page, left to the translation PRs. The general code review and security review skills weren't run.

### Potential follow-ups

- Seed discovery from the stored records, and hand gossip only confirmed ones (next PR).
- Expire evidence, once discovery has heard from the network after a restart.

🤖 Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5

topPRs.title: kona-node!: verify L1 RPC data against block headers
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
With an untrusted L1 RPC, kona-node checked only block hashes. A dishonest or buggy L1 RPC could drop batcher transactions or deposits from what derivation sees, or install an unsafe block signer of its choosing, without any error. Unless `--l1-trust-rpc` is set, the node now verifies what it reads through its shared L1 client against the block header, as op-node does: header hashes, block numbers, transactions and receipts roots, and an `eth_getProof` proof of the unsafe block signer.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/568
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/582
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/583

**Stack.** This is part 4 of 5, split out of #23829. Merge them in order:
1. #23846: delete `DerivationDelegateClient`
2. #23847: check sync-start L1 origins against the canonical chain
3. #23848: share one L1 client across the node
4. #23849: verify L1 RPC data against block headers ← this PR
5. #23850: resolve pipeline reset bases by hash

**Effect on operators**
- With `--l1-trust-rpc=false`, the default, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`, or the node fails to start. The README, the flag help and the operator docs now say so.
- The chain provider's cache metrics replace the `block_info_and_transactions` value of the `cache` label with `transactions`. The bundled dashboards are unaffected.
- The L1 watcher waits a full poll interval after each poll, so a slow L1 RPC is not polled again as soon as it answers.

Until the reset-by-hash PR above this one removes it, the pipeline reset's separate lookup by number goes through the same verification as every other lookup.

**For reviewers.** Each commit is self-contained and builds and passes on its own. Each `!` commit's message states what breaks and how to migrate. Read in this order:
- verification, from `1b33bce8ea` to `eca5df16df`, then `ae0ab3940b`;
- the review fixes, from `6ac3383d08`;
- the docs, `f6ed432cdc` and `d7b86a68ed`.

**Reviews.** On #23829, I ran `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer` and a security review of the L1 verification against op-node over these commits. Here they are unchanged, except that the reset lookup is routed through verification; `rust-code-reviewer` checked that change. I skipped `deposit-reviewer` and `derivation-batch-reviewer`, because nothing here changes how deposits or batches are decoded. Finding dismissed, with the author's agreement:
- **Two cleanups are left for later:** a shared `BlockInfo`-from-header constructor, and one helper for mapping a missing block to `None`.

Older gaps the reviews found are tracked in protocol-team: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/570, https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/571 and https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/572. The L2 provider's verification is https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/569.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects operators, dashboards and code that uses the `kona-providers-alloy` crate.
- **Operators:** without `--l1-trust-rpc`, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`.
- **Dashboards and alerts:** queries on the chain provider's cache metrics that filter on `cache="block_info_and_transactions"` must use `cache="transactions"`.
- **Rust API:** `AlloyChainProviderError` gains `HeaderHashMismatch`, `BlockNumberMismatch`, `TransactionsRootMismatch`, `ReceiptsRootMismatch` and `InvalidStorageProof`, and `EmptyRawReceiptsForNonEmptyBlock` loses its `transaction_count` field. `AlloyChainProvider::unsafe_block_signer` returns `Result<Address, AlloyChainProviderError>`. `AlloyChainProvider::latest_block_number` and `AlloyChainProvider::chain_id` are removed.

Each `!` commit's message gives the exact change and the migration.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: kona-node!: share one L1 client across the node
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
kona-node read L1 through several separately built clients. Derivation, the sequencer, the L1 watcher, the engine and the unsafe block signer lookup each had their own connection, caches and timeouts, so the same L1 data was fetched and cached more than once, and some reads had no deadline. The node now builds one `AlloyChainProvider` at startup and shares it, so every L1 read goes through the same caches and one per-request deadline on the transport. This also gives L1 verification, in the next PR, a single place to live. The engine's sync-start check now reads the canonical L1 block by number through the shared client.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23745
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/579
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/580
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/581

**Stack.** This is part 3 of 5, split out of #23829. Merge them in order:
1. #23846: delete `DerivationDelegateClient`
2. #23847: check sync-start L1 origins against the canonical chain
3. #23848: share one L1 client across the node ← this PR
4. #23849: verify L1 RPC data against block headers
5. #23850: resolve pipeline reset bases by hash

**Effect on operators.** Nothing changes in what the node checks or what the L1 RPC must serve. The L1 metrics change:
- L1 RPC metrics come from the transport. `kona_providers_chain_rpc_calls` and `kona_providers_chain_rpc_errors` are replaced by `kona_rpc_client_request_duration_seconds{client, method, outcome, error}`. Its `method` label holds JSON-RPC method names, and failures that are not RPC errors, such as receipts that fail to decode, are no longer counted as errors.
- `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes`, which nothing set, is removed.
- The chain provider's cache metrics use new `cache` label values.
- The bundled dashboards are updated.

**For reviewers.** Each commit is self-contained and builds and passes on its own. Each `!` commit's message states what breaks and how to migrate. Read in this order:
- the shared client, from `e48420165c` to `71436310ff`;
- follow-ups to the provider's API, from `968103fdf4` to `ed8eefe1a2` (`213f446544` only ignores local Zed settings);
- caching and metrics, from `d51bac140e` to `9d86fb8c65`.

**Reviews.** These are #23829's commits, rebased past the moved reset change, plus a test helper that keeps kona-rpc's tests compiling at each commit. On #23829, `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer` and `safedb-reviewer` ran over them. Findings dismissed, with the author's agreement:
- **The dashboard panel for `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` is kept.** It was already empty before this PR.
- **The request deadline comes from the transport kona-node builds, not from `AlloyChainProvider` itself.** The requirement is documented on `L1ConfigBuilder::provider` and `AlloyChainProvider::new`. Moving the deadline into the provider crate can follow separately.
- **`kona-engine` now depends on `kona-providers-alloy`.** This is intended: the engine reads L1 through the shared client.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects dashboards, alerts and code that uses kona's Rust crates.
- **Dashboards and alerts:** they must move to the metrics above.
- **Rust API:**
  - `kona-providers-alloy`: `AlloyChainProvider`'s constructors (`new_http` and the two-argument `new` are removed, and `cache_size` is a `NonZeroUsize`), its `inner` and `trust_rpc` are no longer public, the free `unsafe_block_signer` function is removed, and the `Metrics` constants for RPC calls, errors and cache memory are removed or renamed.
  - `kona-node-service`: `L1Config`, `L1ConfigBuilder`, `BlockStream`, `L1WatcherActor`, `DelayedL1OriginSelectorProvider`, `L1OriginSelectorError`, `EngineConfig` and `build_engine_client`.
  - `kona-engine`: the L1 methods on `EngineClient` and `EngineClientBuilder`, and a new `SyncStartError::L1` variant.

Each `!` commit's message gives the exact change and the migration.

topPRs.title: op-reth: add an opt-in sweep prune for the proofs-history index
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
Follows #24075.

With page-cache warming on, the prune of the history index is the largest part of what persisting a proofs-history block still costs. A prune removes the pruned blocks from the index key by key: for every key those blocks changed, it looks up the key's first shard and rewrites it. On op-mainnet that is about 1,070 lookups per block in random places of four B-trees: 94 of 208 ms and 89 of 105 disk reads per block. Each rewrite also dirties a page that the commit has to write. This PR adds a mode in which a prune leaves those block numbers in the index and cleans a short run of neighbouring rows instead.

Effect on operators: none by default. `--proofs-history.sweep-prune` (default off) changes how a prune cleans the history index:
- A prune only deletes the changesets of the pruned blocks. Their block numbers stay in the index. Reads do not change: a lookup takes the first block number above the block it reads at, and no block before the proof window is read.
- Each prune cleans a share of each history table in key order, in proportion to the blocks it prunes, so that a full pass takes about one proof window of blocks. On op-mainnet that is about 75 rows per block.
- The index grows, because a block number stays in it for up to one more proof window.
- A database pruned this way cannot be backfilled, also after the flag is turned off: `op-reth proofs backfill` refuses it.
- `reth_optimism_trie_storage_history_unique_keys` reports the rows a sweep visited under `operation="sweep"` and has no `operation="prune"` series while the flag is on. The phase duration and page-fault metrics keep `operation="prune"`.

Measured on three op-mainnet followers with production hardware (devnets-private#2644), on the same 126,000 blocks over 70 hours at the tip. Both nodes with warming use 8 threads:

| | no warming | warming | warming and sweep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Persistence per block | 1,069 ms | 208 ms | 79 ms |
| Write, prune, commit | 356, 640, 74 ms | 32, 94, 81 ms | 31, 6, 43 ms |
| Disk reads the persistence thread waits on, per block | 1,574 | 105 | 23 |
| Disk write operations of the node, per block | 5,415 | 5,389 | 3,018 |
| Proofs readable after the block's timestamp, median and p99 | 4.9 s, 235 s | 1.03 s, 2.65 s | 0.40 s, 1.81 s |
| Most blocks behind the tip | 226 | 5 | 5 |

Per day the node with the sweep took 77, 81 and 83 ms per block. Its prune and commit stayed flat. The rise is in the write step, which rose the same on the node with warming only. The slowest single batch of the 70 hours was on the node with the sweep: readable 12.2 s after its block, against 8.4 s on the node with warming only. Its write and commit were long; its prune was not.

What these numbers do not show:
- The steady state. The node is 22% into its first pass, so the sweep still finds fewer block numbers to remove per row than it will later, and its page writes can still rise. Its four history tables are 34.1 GiB against 29.0 GiB (+18%), and the gap is still growing. A projection for a full pass, not a measurement: 6 to 13 GiB more than without the sweep, about 1% of the 1,050 GiB database.
- `eth_getProof` latency on the node with the sweep, the sweep without warming, and other chains or disks.
- The code after review. The numbers come from revision `928514e3` of branch `jelias2/op-reth-proofs-history-sweep`: this change on the warming code before its review. Since then a warming prune pass reads 16 blocks at a time, and the review of this PR changed the per-key prune and the handling of an unreadable position, both described below. The sweep reads and writes the same rows.

Choices the diff does not explain:
- Backfill is refused, not fixed. Backfill moves the start of the window back. A block number that the sweep has not removed yet is then inside the window again, without a changeset, for any key that the backfilled block's diff does not rewrite, and that key reads wrong without an error. Making backfill safe needs a full sweep before it, or proof that backfill and the live path record the same keys per block. The docs tell operators to backfill before they enable the flag.
- `V2HistorySweepProgress` is both the position of the sweep and the mark that a database has been swept. The position is written in the prune's transaction, so it cannot disagree with the rows, and it is written also when the sweep stands at the first row or the table is empty. Backfill checks the table, not the flag, so the refusal survives turning the flag off.
- The per-key prune changes too, for every database: it removes every block number up to the end of its range from the keys it visits, not only the numbers inside the range. On a database that was never swept that is the same set, because a per-key prune leaves no number below its range. On a swept database with the flag turned off again, the numbers the sweep left would otherwise never go, and every later prune of a busy key would walk over all of that key's old shards again.
- A saved position that cannot be decoded starts the sweep at the first row again, with a warning. Returning the error would fail that prune and every one after it, and the prune shares its transaction with the block writes.
- A read below the start of the window gives another result than before, and nothing makes such a read: with a block number left in the index it finds the key absent, where it found the value at the start of the window. The RPC checks the window in the transaction it reads in (`rpc/src/state.rs`), and the audit below found no other caller that reads below the window.
- Warming skips its per-key history reads for a prune that sweeps, and does not warm the sweep. The sweep reads a run of neighbouring rows, about 6 disk reads per block.

Reviews: four agents reviewed the change before this PR: `rust-code-reviewer`, a correctness audit (every reader and writer of the history tables, append, unwind, backfill, turning the flag on and off, the cursor handling), a test-coverage review, and a comment and docs review. The audit found no path to a wrong read, a crash or lost data. Fixed from them: the per-key prune over a swept history and the unreadable position (both above), the sweep's stats now go through the prune's `step` helper, a method that shared its name with a field, the metric's help text, comments, and the docs section (unreleased callout, when to enable, measured cost). New tests: the share per prune, the mark on an emptied table, a saved row that was the last one, an unreadable position, the per-key prune after a sweep, the refusal with the flag off, an unwind over a key whose shards two sweeps split, the warming skip and the metric label. The bound on how long a block number waits is now one window; it allowed two. Seven of these tests were checked by breaking the code they cover (the per-key filter, the fallback, the warming skip, the label, the cap on the share, the write of the mark, the speed of the sweep): each failed.

No separate security review: the change adds one boolean flag and no input surface.

The Korean pages under `docs/public-docs/ko` do not document the new flag yet.

Dismissed, with the author's confirmation:
- `provider_rw` builds the provider with a struct literal instead of a `with_history_sweep` builder on the provider. The literal is in the module that owns the struct, and a builder would be new API for one caller.
- Helpers in `sweep_tests.rs` repeat helpers that are private to a module in `tests.rs`. Sharing them means moving helpers out of existing tests; each test file of the crate carries its own today.
- The casts in `sweep_history_share`. Neither can truncate: a row count widens to `u64`, and `rows` is at most that count.
- A note that renaming a history table orphans its saved position. A rename needs a migration of the table anyway, and the sweep would start again at the first row.
- A named helper for "this history was swept" in backfill. It has one use, with the reason in a comment at the call.
- In sweep mode the prune still collects the keys of the changesets it deletes, which only the per-key path reads. Removing that changes the signatures of the four changeset prunes; the reviewer said to leave it.
- No test that the flag reaches the store from `launch_node`. `launch_node` has no unit tests and its storage setup would have to be split out; the warming flag is wired the same way. A break turns the sweep off, which is the default behaviour, and shows as a missing `operation="sweep"` series.
- No direct sweep test on the storage tables. The four key types have fixed-length encodings, the saved position is compared as encoded bytes, and the tests that prune through the store sweep and resume all four tables.
- The backfill error gives no remedy. There is none for that database; the docs say to backfill before enabling the flag.
- Backfill refuses a swept database at its first block, after `run_with_snapshot` has built its snapshot. Refusing earlier needs a new method on the backfill traits, which every store wrapper would have to forward.
- Cursor constructors accept a block below the window. This PR does not change that; the callers check.

topPRs.title: kona-peers,kona-disc!: Save the bootstore reliably
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

kona-node now saves its bootstore, saves it safely, and stops at startup when it can't, instead of running with a store it never saves. First PR of a stack for #23767; the next one changes *what* the bootstore saves.

For operators:
- The bootstore is saved at the default path, `~/.kona/<chain_id>/bootstore.json`, or at `--p2p.bootstore`. A missing file and its directory are created at startup.
- The node doesn't start if the bootstore file can't be read, isn't a JSON list of records, or is missing and can't be created. Entries that aren't node records are logged at WARN and dropped.
- The file is replaced atomically, only when its records changed, with the mode a newly created file gets.
- New counter `kona_node_discovery_dropped_enrs`: session records dropped because the channel to gossip was full. `kona_node_enr_store_time` now records only saves that wrote the file.
- The `kona-node` docker recipe keeps the bootstore in the node's home: its `kona_data` volume is mounted at `/home/app`, and `--p2p.bootstore` is gone.

BREAKING CHANGE: kona-node no longer starts when its bootstore can't be read, isn't a JSON list of records, or is missing and can't be created; before, it silently kept the records in memory and lost them at every restart. This applies to the default path too, so a node without `--p2p.bootstore` needs a writable home directory. Point `--p2p.bootstore` at a file, not a directory (such as `/db/bootstore.json` instead of `/db`), delete a file that isn't a bootstore, or pass `--p2p.no-bootstore`. In the kona-peers and kona-disc APIs, `BootStore::open`, `BootStore::in_memory` and `BootStoreFile::path` replace the `From`/`TryInto` conversions, `Default`, and the public fields; `BootStore::sync` returns whether there were changes; `merge` and `valid_peers` are gone; `Discv5Driver::bootstore` is an opened `BootStore`.

### Why

The bootstore usually wasn't saved at all. A failed open fell back to a store kept only in memory, without a log. Nothing created the default path's directory, and our docker recipes passed a directory as the path, so after a restart the node only had its bootnodes to start from; #24094 found that on Sepolia only one operator's built-in bootnodes answer. Where a file was saved, it was rewritten every minute by truncating it first, so a reader could see it empty and a crash left it empty. The driver also handed records to gossip from spawned tasks that waited for room in the channel, which piled up while gossip fell behind, and inbound sessions decide how many there are.

### How

- `BootStore` is a path, a private `Records` type with just the file's contents, and a dirty flag. `open` only reads, so that tests and tools can read the file while the node saves it. `Discv5Builder::build` opens it and saves it, which creates a missing file, so the node finds out at startup whether it can.
- Saves write a temporary file next to the bootstore, `fsync` it and rename it over the bootstore, on a blocking thread that the driver waits for.
- Records go to gossip with `try_send` from the driver loop. Saved records are shuffled, so each store interval gets a different part of them through, and fill at most half of the channel, leaving the rest for session records, which are handed over only once.

### Caveats

- An existing, valid bootstore in a directory the node can't write doesn't stop it from starting; every save then fails with a WARN. A file that exists was written by the node, so startup only checks a missing one.
- A symlinked `bootstore.json` is replaced by a regular file at the first save. A crash during a save can leave a `bootstore.json.*.tmp` behind. The directory isn't synced after the rename, so after a power loss the file may be the one from before the save.
- I couldn't run the docker recipe locally. Unrelated to this PR, it mounts the JWT at `/root/jwt` while the image runs as user 10001, which may not be able to read it.

### Alternatives

- Checking in `open` that the directory is writable, with a throwaway temporary file: rejected, as readers open the store too, and opening shouldn't write.
- Making the recipe's `/db` volume writable with a one-off service that `chown`s it as root: rejected as awkward next to mounting the node's home, which the image already owns.
- Review agents run: `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer`, and a general correctness and security review. Each finding fixed has its own commit. Dismissed:
  - the writability of an existing file (first caveat);
  - duplicate entries, or entries beyond 2048, in a hand-edited file don't mark the store dirty, so they stay in the file until the next change: the next PR reworks how records are added and can report these with the skipped ones;
  - the symlink, leftover temporary file and directory sync caveats above;
  - the "ENR Store Time" Grafana panel only sampling saves that wrote, which is intended;
  - the dev recipe's Dockerfile copying a Sepolia seed to a path nothing reads, which predates this PR;
  - the Korean configuration page, left to the translation-drift PRs.

### Follow-ups

- The rest of #23767, as stacked PRs: save only records that an outbound gossip connection verified, keep evidence timestamps per record and evict by them, and seed discovery from the saved records; then expire stale records.

Part of #23767.

🤖 Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5
